The rule says a tenant must not paint a wall on a day if there is no approval of that tenant happening on or before that day. Ben's approval happened on 5 January 2027, which is no later than 7 January 2027. So the condition for the prohibition is not met on 7 January, and the text imposes no prohibition then. The text doesn't say anything about whether painting is required or permitted beyond that; it simply doesn't forbid it on that day.

Option D says "permitted," which is a reasonable reading of the absence of a prohibition, and it adds that the text doesn't say whether it is required. Option E says the text says nothing about it. The rule does address that day, because its condition is evaluated and found not to apply, so the prohibition does not hold. Under ordinary reading, not being forbidden means it is permitted, and nothing makes it required.

ANSWER: D
